title: Rome Cracks Down on Tourist Golf Carts
paragraphs: Golf carts have become a common sight in central Rome, carrying tourists along cobblestone streets and between famous landmarks. But their rapid growth has brought complaints about traffic, illegal parking and overtourism — and city officials are getting ready to act.
Bookings for golf cart tours rose by 147% this summer compared with 2024, according to Tripadvisor. Rome may now have as many as 500 carts.

The tours appeal to visitors who want to see several major attractions in just a few hours. Supporters say electric carts are quiet, take up less space than tour buses and vans, and produce no exhaust fumes that can damage historic monuments.
Critics, however, say they add to congestion in an already crowded city center. Drivers also frequently park illegally because Rome has no designated spots for golf carts.
Parking was already a problem before the carts arrived. Cars, vans and scooters regularly occupy curbs, crosswalks and traffic islands, while delivery trucks often double-park.

Regulating the carts has proved difficult. Different models are covered by different transport rules, while tourism and passenger services are controlled by the Lazio regional government rather than Rome itself.

Rome has asked the regional government to hand over authority to regulate the industry. If approved, Deputy Mayor Eugenio Patanè plans to introduce fixed tour routes, limit the number of carts and decide which companies can operate them.
Tour companies argue that the proposed rules could severely damage their industry. They also say the current lack of clear rules has led to inconsistent and sometimes harsh punishments.
Carts accused of operating as unlicensed private-hire vehicles can be banned from the streets for over a month. Drivers can also be fined $4,600 for conducting tours without the required license.
Golf cart driver Martin Halili believes the industry is being singled out following complaints from taxi drivers and other competitors.
"They have waged a war against us," he said. "They have it in for golf carts."
